ratings.concept: Point defects in ionic solids: Frenkel is a dislocation defect that leaves the density unchanged, Schottky is a vacancy defect that lowers it
ratings.strategy_evidence: The single fact that a Frenkel defect displaces an ion to an interstitial site WITHIN the crystal, removing nothing, fixes the density as unchanged for Frenkel and lowered for Schottky; that one fact strikes out options 3 and 4 together, since each attaches the other defect's density behaviour to its own.

traps.label: other_one_fact
traps.route: attaches to Frenkel the host that belongs to the other member of the pair: alkali halides such as NaCl and KCl show SCHOTTKY defects, while Frenkel defects are shown by silver halides and ZnS, where the cation is much smaller than the anion

traps.label: other_one_fact
traps.route: attaches to Schottky the density behaviour that belongs to Frenkel: it is the Frenkel defect that has no effect on density, because nothing leaves the crystal, whereas Schottky removes a cation-anion pair and so lowers the density

traps.label: other_one_fact
traps.route: the mirror image of option 3 - attaches to Frenkel the density decrease that belongs to Schottky; the Frenkel ion is relocated and not removed, so the mass and the volume are both unchanged

ratings.reason: This question requires holding two neighbouring defect types apart on three separate counts, demonstrated by the four options, which pair the words Frenkel and Schottky with density, host lattice and dislocation in every combination but one.
ratings.note: Option 2 as stored reads "halides of alkaline metals"; alkali metals are meant. The term as printed does not change the verdict, since neither alkali nor alkaline-earth halides are the Frenkel hosts, but it is recorded because it is a wording defect rather than a chemistry one.

ratings.concept: Coordination number from denticity (en and oxalate are both bidentate) and oxidation state from charge balance including the ionisable counter-ion
ratings.strategy_evidence: Two bidentate en ligands and one bidentate oxalate give a coordination number of six on their own, so the sum asked for must exceed six; that single fact strikes out option 4, which prints 6.

traps.label: intermediate_value
traps.route: prints the coordination number by itself: 6 is the correct result of the first of the two determinations, and the oxidation number is then not added to it

traps.label: wrong_quantity
traps.route: adds the wrong quantity to the coordination number: 7 is 6 + 1, where 1 is the charge on the complex ION [M(en)2(C2O4)]+, not the oxidation number of the metal; the two quantities differ by the oxalate's -2

traps.label: omitted_contribution
traps.route: 8 is 6 + 2, which is what the charge balance gives when the ionisable chloride outside the coordination sphere is left out of the sum; without that -1 the metal comes out as +2 instead of +3

ratings.reason: This question requires applying two separate conventions to one printed formula, demonstrated by the stem's "[M(en)2(C2O4)]Cl (Where en is ethylenediamine)", from which the denticities give six and the chloride outside the brackets gives +3.

ratings.concept: Addition-elimination of carbonyl compounds with ammonia derivatives: hydrazine adds and then loses water to give a hydrazone, while HCN, bisulphite and Grignard reagents stop at the addition product
ratings.strategy_evidence: Only the nitrogen nucleophiles of the ammonia-derivative family lose water after adding to a carbonyl group; hydrazine is the only such reagent printed, so that one fact strikes out options 1, 2 and 3 together.

traps.label: half_true
traps.route: the stem names two requirements and hydrocyanic acid meets the first: it does add nucleophilically to the carbonyl carbon. The requirement that fails is the second - the cyanohydrin retains its OH group and no water is eliminated

traps.label: half_true
traps.route: sodium hydrogen sulphite likewise satisfies "nucleophilic addition", giving the crystalline bisulphite adduct, and fails on "elimination of water": the adduct keeps both the OH and the SO3- group

traps.label: half_true
traps.route: a Grignard reagent satisfies the addition half and fails the elimination half: the alkoxide formed is protonated on work-up to an alcohol, so water is added rather than eliminated

ratings.reason: This question requires applying a two-part mechanistic criterion to four reagents, demonstrated by the stem's "nucleophilic addition followed by elimination of water", where every option satisfies the first clause and only hydrazine satisfies the second.

group_note: All six were read as the same printed shape - one question, four answers, no lettered block or printed list - and two members carry figures that the text alone does not reproduce: 2015_A#q030, whose stem is a bare "[reaction scheme]" placeholder, and 2015_A#q029. Both figures are present and legible, so both questions are complete once read with the figure and neither is treated as damaged; that is said in each note so the text-only rendering gets repaired. Three stated rules kept the group consistent. (1) DEMAND: four members are `application` or `concept_discrimination` on the same test - is the work applying a stated rule to this case, or separating two neighbouring concepts? q028 (one group trend applied to four elements), q031 (two conventions applied to one formula) and q032 (a two-part criterion applied to four reagents) are `application`; q027 (Frenkel against Schottky) and q029 (enantiomers against diastereomers and meso forms) are `concept_discrimination`, because their option sets pair the same two or three concepts with different attributes and nothing is applied to a new case. 2015_A#q030 is the only `recall` member and the reason is specific: a named reaction has to be matched to a printed reagent set, and no rule is applied or concept separated - knowing the name is the whole of it. (2) STRUCTURE: `several_independent_checks` where each option or each requirement is adjudicated separately and the verdicts combined (q027 three defect claims, q031 two separate determinations then summed, q032 four reagents); `single_step` where one fact or one ordering settles it (q028, q029, q030). q031 is the closest call and is deliberately NOT multi_step_dependent: the coordination number and the oxidation state are found independently of each other and only then added, which the rulebook distinguishes from step 2 needing step 1's result. (3) STRATEGY: five of the six carry `elimination`, and each has its one named fact and the options it strikes out written out; q027's shortcut strikes two options with one density fact, q032's strikes three with one family fact. (4) TRAPS: every tagged option names what makes it wrong. The repeated device in q027 is one and the same - a true fact about the OTHER defect - so all three distractors carry `other_one_fact` with the member named, and the uniformity is the construction's, not a default. q028 is the one ordering question and its devices are ordering devices: the exact reverse (`reversed_order`) separated from the two that get an end or an adjacency right (`sequence_endpoint_or_adjacency`), which is precisely the distinction the two labels exist to draw. q032's three distractors share a single structure - each meets the stem's first clause and fails its second - which is `half_true` three times over with the failing clause named. q031 is the member whose numeric options allow three different devices (the bare intermediate, the wrong quantity, the omitted term) and that is why it differs from the rest.
